assessment.rationale: Simulated all 12 allowed pressure/shelf pairs from the native knownRp configuration in source LyoPRONTO-native-case:LPN-3051800662 (no internal process models used). Constraints: vial-bottom temperature at or below the critical product temperature -30 C, and whole-batch sublimation rate within the equipment line -0.182 + 11.7*P kg/h. Whole-batch rate = native peak flux (kg/h/m2) x total product area (9000 vials x 3.14 cm2 = 2.826 m2). Eleven candidates violate at least one constraint: every shelf setting at 10 and -5 C, and every 0.2 Torr pair, exceeds -30 C in max returned vial-bottom temperature (warmest -17.25 C); every 0.05 Torr pair exceeds its 0.403 kg/h line (peak 0.808 kg/h even at -25 C shelf); 0.1 Torr at -15, -5 and 10 C exceed their 0.988 kg/h line (1.209-2.474 kg/h) and the temperature limit. The only pair satisfying both is 0.1 Torr / -25 C shelf: 100% dried at 32.67 h (within the 60 h horizon), max returned vial-bottom -31.225 C (thermal margin 1.225 C below the limit), peak native flux 0.25080 kg/h/m2 giving peak whole-batch 0.7088 kg/h vs 0.988 kg/h line (capacity margin 0.279 kg/h). Fastest feasible = only feasible. Authored simulator-world characterization (no experimental measurements): constraint checks are on returned solver nodes with no continuous-maximum guarantee, forward mode does not enforce limits, and agreement is not experimental validation.

output.content:
**Selected recipe: 0.1 Torr chamber pressure with a −25 °C shelf — the only one of the 12 allowed pairs that satisfies both constraints, so it is also the fastest feasible one.** Predicted complete drying at 32.67 h (returned 100% dried at 32.670 h, inside the 60 h horizon).

**The two constraint margins** (from the native run, whole-batch rate = peak flux × 2.826 m² product area from 9,000 vials × 3.14 cm²):

- **Thermal:** max returned vial-bottom temperature −31.23 °C vs the −30 °C critical → **1.23 °C below the limit**.
- **Equipment line:** peak whole-batch sublimation 0.709 kg/h (0.2508 kg/h/m² × 2.826 m²) vs the line −0.182 + 11.7 × 0.1 = 0.988 kg/h → **0.279 kg/h headroom**.

**Why every other pair fails:** all four 0.05 Torr pairs exceed their 0.403 kg/h line (peaks 0.808–2.324 kg/h); all four 0.2 Torr pairs exceed the −30 °C bottom limit (max −28.97 to −17.25 °C, and the 10 °C shelf also breaks its 2.158 kg/h line at 2.734 kg/h); at 0.1 Torr, the −15, −5 and 10 °C shelves break both limits (bottom −26.95 to −19.47 °C; 1.209–2.474 kg/h vs 0.988).

**Saved:** the assessment is recorded as a draft requiring review, with all twelve native simulation runs attached to source LPN-3051800662; it is not a manufacturing approval, and no measured outcome is implied. No internal process models were used.

**What I could not check:** the constraint checks use returned solver nodes only, with no continuous-maximum guarantee — I did not rerun a denser time grid, so a between-node bottom temperature above −30 °C or a higher peak flux cannot be ruled out; a finer-grid rerun would settle both margins. This is a synthetic authored characterization case, so agreement with the same equations is not validation.
